newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot gas prices rise again on hot weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot gas prices rise again on hot weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices rose another couple of cents Thursday as heat and sporadic plant outages in the Southwest continued to keep supplies tight, industry sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast gas at the Henry Hub traded about one cent higher at $2.21-2.24 per mmBtu.
South Texas prices were equally firmer at $2.11-2.14 as temperatures in Houston were expected to climb into the low-90s F through this weekend.
Also, Houston Lighting and Power's 1,250 megawatt (MW) South Texas 1 nuclear unit was reduced to 80 percent power.
Power reduction at the unit was expected to be short-lived, but the utility said no specific time frame was available.
In the East, New York city gate prices were talked at $2.45-2.47, up one to three cents from Wednesday.
Temperatures in the Northeast were forecast to hover near a high of 90 degrees F on Saturday, Weather Services Corp reported.
In the Midwest, prices gained another two cents to about $2.07-2.08, with Chicago city-gate quoted in the mid-$2.20s.
Temperatures in Chicago were expected to reach a high of 87 degrees F on Friday, followed by a high of 81 degrees F on Saturday amid rain showers, WSC said.
In west Texas, Permian prices rose by about two cents to $2.06-2.11 as temperatures in southern California still reached highs in the mid-80s F.
Southern California prices also gained a few cents to $2.25-2.27, while San Juan prices for non-constrained gas stretched to $2.03-2.10, traders said.
The outage at El Paso Natural Gas Co's Blanco natural gas plant in the San Juan basin continued, expected to cut about 240 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of gas on Friday and Saturday.

Adding to the bullish sentiment, traders said, was news that the 1,080 megawatt (MW) San Onofre 2 nuclear unit would not restart late next week as scheduled. Southern California Edison said a new date was set for around July 10.
Conversely, the 750 MW Mohave 1 coal-fired unit in Nevada returned to service today after shutting down last Saturday, a plant spokesman said.
Also resuming power were the two 750 MW units at the Moss Landing natural gas plant near Monterey, Calif., Pacific Gas and Electric reported.
